blind_target.title: Gender-Biased Breastfeeding in Egypt: Examining the Fertility Preference Hypotheses of Jayachandran and Kuziemko (2011).
blind_target.evidence_quote:
Further, according to the fourth prediction (Chakravarty 2015), we may
expect the effect of children’s sex composition on breastfeeding duration to
be different for boys and girls. The results in the last column of table 5 are in-
deed consistent with Chakravarty (2015); girls are breastfed for an additional

blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Additional sex-composition prediction is supported; birth-order result is obtained with the original specification but rejected after adding the omitted gender main effect. Both findings are explicitly retested.

prior_decision.location: Section V.F-G, p. 206 (lines 1394-1403); see also Section V.C, p. 199 (lines 1043-1048), Section V.F, p. 205 (lines 1344-1352), and Section VII, p. 212 (lines 1751-1755)
prior_decision.reason: Chakravarty (2015) is a replicated target tested on two components in the Pakistan DHS sample: (1) Chakravarty's additional sibling-sex-composition hypothesis (prediction 4, eq. 3), which is confirmed in Table 5 col. 5 (Section V.C), Section V.G, and the Conclusion (Section VII), and (2) Chakravarty's quadratic birth-order interaction specification for prediction 9 (Section V.F, Table 9 cols. 2-3). In Table 9 col. 2, replicating Chakravarty's original specification reproduces a strongly statistically significant gender-by-birth-order interaction (p = .000 jointly) in line with a middle-birth-order peak, but the authors show that Chakravarty's specification omits the gender main effect and that adding the gender dummy in col. 3 eliminates the middle-birth-order peak. Under the codebook's main-message rule, 'statistically successful but flawed' applies only when the methodological critique is the paper's main message; here, the omitted-main-effect critique concerns only one regression specification in Section V.F and is not the main message of the paper or of the Chakravarty comparison (which highlights confirmation of prediction 4 in the Summary and Conclusion). Because prediction 4 is supported while the middle-birth-order peak is rejected once properly specified, the overall outcome for Chakravarty (2015) is 'mixed'.

luna_triage.reason: The paper explicitly tests Chakravarty (2015)'s additional prediction and reports results from it; the full text also retests Chakravarty's birth-order specification. The only supplied shipped original, Jayachandran and Kuziemko (2011), is a different paper and cannot represent Chakravarty (2015). The retested findings concern child sex composition and birth-order patterns in breastfeeding duration.
